explanation: Compared against A. Fanelli and L. Moscardelli, 'Approximately Stable Matching' (ECAI 2025, doi:10.3233/FAIA251234, open-access PDF), Sections 2 and 5. Model: agents rank neighbours and themselves with rank_i(i) = δ_i + 1 (single is worst); a matching is an involution with fixed points single; {i,j} ∈ E is k-blocking at m if rank_i(m(i)) − rank_i(j) ≥ k and rank_j(m(j)) − rank_j(i) ≥ k; k ≥ 1. Roommates.CompleteProfile/partnerRank/IsKBlockingPair/IsKStable with the complete graph ⊤ reproduce this exactly (one-based ranks, self ranked n), and stabilityThreshold N is the least k ≥ 1 such that every complete profile on N agents has a k-stable matching (existence is monotone in k, so this is the threshold). Section 5: 'Theorem 1 shows existence (and convergence) for k = ⌈|N|/2⌉ ... exhaustive search on all complete graphs with up to |N| = 6 nodes ... k = ⌈|N|/2⌉ − 1 does not suffice ... We conjecture that the lower bound can be improved and that ⌈|N|/2⌉ could represent the true threshold even for larger values of |N|.' The value (N+1)/2 in ℕ is ⌈N/2⌉, correct (the ceilings are confirmed by Theorem 2's k = ⌊(n−3)/2⌋ + 1 = ⌈n/2⌉ − 1). Discrepancy: the paper's conjecture reads as 'the threshold is ⌈|N|/2⌉ for every |N|' (verified by them for |N| ≤ 6, conjectured beyond), whereas the Lean statement only asserts it for all N ≥ N₀ for some unspecified N₀ (the extra conjunct 3 ≤ N₀ is vacuous, since N₀ can always be increased). The Lean statement is therefore a priori weaker than the conjecture (it would remain true if the formula failed at finitely many N ≥ 7); a proof of the Lean statement would not settle the conjecture as stated, though a disproof would refute it. A faithful version would be ∀ N, stabilityThreshold N = (N + 1) / 2 (true for N = 0? stabilityThreshold 0 = 1 ≠ 0, so ∀ N ≥ 1).
